GOAL prove putnam_2025_b6 without sorry.

FACT The file has one `sorry`, and the set is `{r | ∃ g, ...}` with claimed greatest element `1/4`.

INFER membership_1_4 <- g(n) = n^2. Then g(g n)^(1/4) = (n^4)^(1/4) = n, and g(n+1) - g(n) = 2n+1 ≥ n. So `1/4` is in the set. This part is easy.

HYP upper_bound: every admissible r satisfies r ≤ 1/4.

PLAN prove upper_bound by contradiction, assuming r > 1/4 and a g exists.

FACT g is strictly increasing on positive integers, since g(g n)^r > 0 forces g(n+1) > g(n). Also g(n) ≥ n.

FACT Power-law heuristic: if g(n) ≈ n^p, the constraint needs p ≥ 1 + p²r, so r ≤ 1/4. This gives the right threshold, but only if g is already known to be polynomially bounded above.

FACT Bootstrapping lower bounds (g(n) ≥ c·n^p ⇒ g(n) ≳ n^(1+p²r)) pushes the exponent to infinity when r > 1/4. Superpolynomial lower growth is not itself contradictory, though. The contradiction needs an upper bound on g, which the constraint does not supply directly.

RESULT I have not found a Lean-feasible argument for the upper bound. Formalizing the bootstrap plus the missing upper-bound step needs substantial real-analysis work with rpow and finite sums, and I have not closed that gap.

RESULT The file `/work/putnam_2025_b6.lean` is unchanged. Compiling it was not attempted, because a partial proof would still contain `sorry`.

I give up.
